ObjectName.value: Bus window ruined by sticker

Categories.value: CC-Zero|Stickers in Taiwan|Sunlight through windows in Taiwan|Self-published work|Files with coordinates missing SDC location of creation|Chinese-language stickers|Bus windows in Taiwan|Windows in Taichung|Obscured windows|Vehicle window signs in Taiwan

ImageDescription.value:
Riders cannot see out the window anymore.

This Taiwan public bus funding sticker ends up blocking the view. It announces to people outside the bus, that this bus has public funding, but at the same time totally ignores the rights of riders to any kind of view at all, not just pleasant views.

The supposedly clear parts are just blurry plastic.

Good news, on June 11, 2024 they changed the rule for future funding stickers. They will be stuck next to the right side rear lights:

交通部公路局已於113年6月11日修正「交通部補助電動大客車作業要點」規定，交通部補助電動大客車之補助標示貼紙位置，應張貼於車尾右下角車燈旁。

115231760.title: File:Light spectrum on a wall caused by sunlight going through prism and then handmade glass.jpg

ObjectName.value: Light spectrum on a wall caused by sunlight going through prism and then handmade glass

Categories.value: Visible spectrum|Prisms (optics)|Self-published work|Images with extracted images|Rainbow lighting|Sunlight through glass

ImageDescription.value:
Scattered resp. distorted light spectrum on a wall - caused by sunlight going through a glass crystal (acting as an optical prism) at a window, and then after c. 6 meters, through the lampshade of a candleholder having an irregular thickness. Size of this spectrum on the wall from bottom to top only about 7 cm, hence the image is strongly enlarged.

The whole phenomenon was not intended, but resulted coincidentally from the positions of the items in the room on a sunny day. Due to the earth rotation, the spectrum on the wall disappeared after only some minutes during which the pictures were taken, and was since never observed again.

14397153.title: File:St Andrew's church - winter sunlight through stained glass window - geograph.org.uk - 1634087.jpg

ObjectName.value: St Andrew's church - winter sunlight through stained glass window - geograph.org.uk - 1634087

Categories.value: Taken with Canon PowerShot S3 IS|Images from Geograph Britain and Ireland|Information field template with formatting|Images by Evelyn Simak|St Andrew's, Barton Bendish (interior)

ImageDescription.value: St Andrew's church - winter sunlight through stained glass window. St Andrew's > 1634049 - 1634070 is the only one of three churches in the village which is still in use. St Mary's church > 1634138 - a couple of hundred metres further to the west - became redundant in 1976 and is now in the care of the Churches Conservation Trust. No traces remain of All Saints church > 1634114 which was situated across the road from St Andrew's. Tower and chancel of St Andrew's church were built in the 14th century, whereas the inner doorway > 1634066 dates from around 1200 and shows a merging of Norman and Gothic styles. The porch > 1634065 with its elaborate flushwork, depicting saltire crosses, was added in the 15th century. The church was restored in the 19th century and the stained glass windows > 1634080 date from that time. There are 17th century box pews on the north wall, one of them with the date 1623 carved into the door > 1634089. The simple octagonal baptismal font is C15 > 1634108. Of particular interest is the chancel > 1634076 floor in that it has retained the complete set of original 4 inch square medieval tiles, decorated with varying patterns > 1634092. And even rarer still is the 14th century piscina > 1634098 with a double drain in the floor below it, which was probably in use during the 13th century when the ritual called for piscinae with two drains. There is no other known example of this combination of two drains in the floor and one in the wall.
